frontier.hypothesis: The next lever is live-range/conflict-graph shape, not source order: check whether `obj`'s live range (read at ~10 sites across the whole loop body) is genuinely wider than target's equivalent value, which would explain why global.c's priority-based coloring picks obj for $s0 over flags in our build but not in target's.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno priority is driven by live-range weight (spill cost x use frequency), not raw declaration/statement order -- consistent with all three killed order-probes this session and last.

frontier.mechanism: split-read-defeats-hoist family (duplicate a read into a branch arm changes a pseudo's live range / conflict set).
